title: Canaries Dashboard: Employment in AI-exposed occupations shrank
summary: The November 2026 Canaries Dashboard release (October data) reports that employment of workers aged 22-25 in jobs with high AI exposure was 4.2% lower than a year earlier, continuing a contraction that began in October 2023 and the largest year-over-year slowdown since November 2025. Employment in the least-exposed jobs for this age group fell 1.3%.
detail: Stanford Digital Economy Lab and ADP Research, Canaries Dashboard, release of 2026-11-18. Same release: high-exposure employment across all ages -0.8% y/y; ages 26-30 high-exposure -3.4%.
reasoning: A deepening year-over-year fall for 22-25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed jobs is the series I-R2-01 resolves on, which bears on the gradual-disempowerment road R2.
counterpoint: The figure is a year-over-year change in an ADP payroll sample, not the index level against its 2026 level that I-R2-01 uses; the release reports employment by AI exposure but does not by itself establish that AI caused the decline, and employment of least-exposed young workers also fell.
